title: Woven or Modular? The Lift-Out Test

zones.label: Woven design
zones.summary: One long page where explanation, quiz, and simulation are threads of one cloth.
facts: Structure: One long page that mixes explanation, a quiz, and a simulation
Taking out the quiz: Copy it from the middle of the page and repair the links.
Revising the simulation: Edit the whole page and risk breaking the reading.
Reuse by another teacher: Take everything or nothing.
Failure phrases: "as we saw in the last section" and "the diagram above".

zones.label: Modular design
zones.summary: A reading, a quiz, and a simulation as separate pieces, each in its own folder.
facts: Structure: Separate pieces: a reading, a quiz, and a simulation.
Taking out the quiz: Link or embed the quiz's own page.
Revising the simulation: Edit the simulation's folder.
Reuse by another teacher: Take any piece.
Modularity is a matter of degree: a single page, a page with sections, one file per part, each part with its own license and metadata.

quiz.question: Which design makes another teacher take everything or nothing?
quiz.explanation: Woven pages cannot be taken apart.

quiz.question: Which design lets you link or embed the quiz's own page?
quiz.explanation: Each piece has its own page.

quiz.question: Which design risks breaking the reading when you revise the simulation?
Which design lets you edit the simulation's folder and leave the rest alone?
quiz.explanation: Each part is in its own folder.
